strategy.summary: Identifying a price action leg to find overlapping PD arrays that act as a First Line of Defense (FLOD) for price rejection, with the swing extreme serving as the Last Line of Defense (LLOD).

timeframes.notes: The concept is theoretically applicable to any timeframe where a clear price action leg exists.

glossary.FLOD: First Line of Defense; the first PD array (often a fair value gap) or overlapping cluster of arrays encountered during a retracement.
glossary.LLOD: Last Line of Defense; the swing extreme (high or low) that defines the origin of the current price action leg.
glossary.Price action lag: The presenter's pronunciation/term for a 'price action leg', defined as the range between a swing high and a swing low.

custom_signals.name: FLOD
custom_signals.plain_definition: The first major PD array encountered in a retracement, providing the highest probability when an FVG overlaps with another array (like an order block).

custom_signals.name: LLOD
custom_signals.plain_definition: The swing high or swing low of the active price action leg, serving as structural invalidation.

sequence: Identify a recent price action leg defined by a clear swing high and swing low.
Map out all premium or discount arrays (FVG, order block, BPR, rejection block) within that leg.
Identify the First Line of Defense (FLOD), which is typically the first FVG that overlaps with another array.
Identify the Last Line of Defense (LLOD), which is the swing extreme of the leg.
Wait for price to retrace into the FLOD. Expect price to reject off this overlapping zone.

invalidation.text: Price breaks and stays beyond the Last Line of Defense (the swing extreme), creating a new opposite price action leg.

filters.text: Avoid taking setups off isolated fair value gaps. The probabilities are significantly higher when the FVG overlaps with another PD array.

entry_rule.text: No explicit entry trigger is defined; implies anticipating a rejection upon retracement into the overlapping PD arrays (FLOD).
entry_rule.quote: when we have that retracement one of those PD arrays should hold

stop_rule.text: No explicit stop rule provided, though the framework dictates that price should not stay beyond the LLOD.
stop_rule.quote: we shouldn't stay below that low

presenter_claims.claim: The first line of defense holding is usually 9 out of 10 times an overlapping pattern, primarily a fair value gap.
High probability conditions (overlapping arrays) have an 80% win rate, while low probability conditions have a 20% win rate.

strategy.notes: This video serves as a structural framework rather than an executable strategy. The presenter strongly emphasizes thinking in probabilities rather than binary outcomes when evaluating setups.
